lines.text: Three kinds of aid: scholarships (usually merit), grants (usually need), and work-study (a paycheck).
lines.say: Scholarships are usually merit gifts, grants are usually need-based gifts, and work-study is a paycheck.
The max Pell Grant for 2026 to 2027 is seven thousand three hundred ninety-five dollars.

lines.text: That max has been flat at $7,395 for four award years in a row.

lines.text: In 2024-25, undergrads averaged $12,080 in grants per full-time-equivalent student (College Board).

lines.text: Example: a $10,000 scholarship puts $3,000 toward housing. That $3,000 is taxable (IRS Pub 970).
lines.say: The catch: say a ten thousand dollar scholarship puts three thousand toward housing. Under IRS rules, that three thousand is taxable.

lines.text: Work-study is earned: at least minimum wage per hour, and the FAFSA leaves that pay out of your income.

post.title: Free college money can still show up on your tax return
post.ig:
Free college money can still show up on your tax return.

Scholarships (usually merit) and grants (usually need) don't have to be repaid. Work-study is a paycheck: at least minimum wage for hours worked.
The max federal Pell Grant is $7,395 for 2026-27, flat for four award years in a row.
Undergrads averaged $12,080 in grant aid per full-time-equivalent student in 2024-25 (College Board).
IRS rule: scholarship money used for housing is taxable. Example: $3,000 of a $10,000 scholarship spent on housing counts as income.

Sources: US Dept. of Education; College Board Trends in Student Aid 2025; IRS Publication 970.
